subject: Reserved capacity commit scope + GPU price-trigger clearance
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@polaris.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@polaris.ai
Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity ask and pricing protection language

Sergio —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re ready to move forward on a reserved capacity commitment but wanted to propose a structure that protects PolarisAI from sharp GPU-market moves. High level: Polaris is comfortable with a 36-month nominal commitment, but we need a mechanism to adjust unit pricing if spot/market GPU costs move >20% in either direction.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) accept a bilateral price-trigger clause tied to a public GPU index, and 2) offer a preliminary tiered discount if we commit to 60% of forecasted peak usage?

We’ve attached a simple scenarios workbook so you can see our sensitivity assumptions.

Attachments: polaris_commit_scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

—Ethan
Ethan Park
Head of Procurement, PolarisAI
[polaris.ai]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@polaris.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask and pricing protection language

Ethan —

Appreciate the clarity. We can support conditional pricing constructs, but need to align internally on what we can approve at the AE level vs. what requires FP&A / legal sign-off.

Quick answers:
- Public-index triggers: possible, but finance will want caps/floors and a reconciliation cadence.
- Tiered discounts at 60% commit: doable as a term-sheet starting point; size of discount depends on the commit tenor and SKU mix.

I’ll pull together a scenario and loop in Kimberly (pricing lead) and Grace (revenue ops) for an internal clearance. We may follow with a short exec sign-off ask if the tiered discount exceeds our standard bands.

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal pricing sensitivity (we’ll review Polaris sheet).
2) Draft contract language with a capped trigger window and monthly reconciliation.
3) Return to you with a redline and exec-approval timeline.

Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_price-trigger-draft.docx]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask and pricing protection language

Team —

I pulled the Polaris scenarios. Two notes up front:
1) If we allow an index-triggered adjustment, we need a defined index (we prefer the public GPU Price Index from GPUWatch) and a bounded band: +/- 25% triggers with a 6-month lookback for reconciliation. Anything wider, and the unit economics become unpredictable.
2) Discount sizing: at 60% committed utilization we can consider a 12–18% off list for A100-class SKUs on a 36-month tenor, provided we include minimum monthly consumption thresholds and a ramp schedule.

If Polaris is asking for a 36-month nominal commitment with a price-trigger, the recommended language:
- Price floor set to 85% of list in case of GPU cost decline cap
- Price cap at 115% of list if GPU market spikes >25% to protect Redwood margin
- Quarterly reconciliation and true-up against the index, with netting each quarter

Anything outside those bounds requires Marissa (Finance) sign-off. I’ll draft a clean AIS (approved internal summary) for exec clearance.

K — Kimberly
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: internal_pricing_note.pdf]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask and pricing protection language

Looping in Karthik for legal/contract constraints. Also flagging renewal engineering impact — if we approve a large discount for an extended tenor we need to reserve headroom in our Dedicated pools for at least the first 18 months.

Karthik — can you confirm whether a bilateral price-trigger tied to a third-party index is acceptable from a contract governance perspective and what the fallback mechanism should be if the index source is unavailable?

Grace
Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-23T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask and pricing protection language

Grace / team —

Legal is OK with index references as long as we: 1) specify the primary and two secondary index sources (GPUWatch index, CloudVendor spot average, and an internal market composite), 2) include an explicit fallback hierarchy, and 3) limit any retroactive adjustments to the quarter following the trigger event. No open-ended retroactive true-ups.

Suggested contract clauses (short):
- "Price Trigger Mechanism": Trigger defined as a 25% move in the agreed composite over a 90-day lookback; parties will reconcile in the next calendar quarter.
- "Index Fallback": If the primary index is unavailable for >14 days, use the secondary; if both unavailable, use Redwood's internal composite published to both parties.
- "Cap on Adjustment": Any upward adjustment cannot exceed 15% in a single quarter and is subject to executive approval above that.

If we want a discount >18% for the 60% baseline, this will require Marissa's written approval and a board-level billing impact review.

Karthik
Chief Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask and pricing protection language

Team —

I reviewed Kimberly and Karthik’s recommendations. Finance can clear: a capped price-trigger construct with the following executive conditions.

Executive clearance summary (approved subject to final contract redline):
- Base discount band: up to 15% for 60% committed utilization over a 36-month tenor.
- Price trigger: +/-25% market movement using the agreed composite, reconciled quarterly. Upward adjustments capped at 12% per quarter without Board escalation.
- Approval gate: any incremental discount beyond 15% or any upward adjustment over 12% in a single quarter requires Director-level sign-off and pre-authorized reserve coverage in our Dedicated pool.
- Operational requirement: Sales to provide a monthly consumption forecast for the first 12 months and a ramp plan; Ops to reserve 20% headroom in capacity for months 1–18.

Sergio — please return to Ethan with the redline and a short note outlining the exec conditions. Also attach the signature block PDF if Polaris is ready to proceed.

Marissa Cole
VP Finance, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: polaris_signature-block.pdf]
